newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen rebel leader due Moscow on Thursday - agency.
newsitem.headline: Chechen rebel leader due Moscow on Thursday - agency.

text.p: Chechen rebel leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev is expected to come to Moscow on Thursday to further a peace settlement for the separatist region, Interfax news agency quoted a spokesman for Russia's Security Council as saying.

Interfax also quoted an unnamed government source as saying that Yandarbiyev, who last visited Moscow to sign a pre-election peace deal with President Boris Yeltsin that subsequently fell apart, might meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Itar-Tass news agency also reported the visit, saying it had been agreed in a meeting between a Security Council representative and rebel spokesman Movladi Udugov in the Chechen capital Grozny.
The administration of the neighbouring Ingushetia region told Interfax they had stepped up security at their airport, from which Yandarbiyev was expected to fly.

Alexander Lebed, secretary of the Security Council, signed a peace deal with rebel chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov at the end of August aimed at ending the conflict, which had dragged on for 21 months.
But the deal has met a lukewarm response in Moscow from Chernomyrdin, who has expressed fears it could play into the hands of the rebels.
